problem: A particle $P$ moves along the $x$-axis in the direction of increasing $x.$ When the displacement of $P$ from the origin $O$ is $x$ meters, the velocity is given by $v(x)={e}^{-2x}\,m/s.$ Initially, $P$ is at the origin $O.$ Find $x$ as a function of time $t.$

feedback.problem: A particle $P$ moves along the $x$-axis in the direction of increasing $x.$ When the displacement of $P$ from the origin $O$ is $x$ meters, the velocity is given by $v(x)=(4-2x)\,m/s.$ Initially, $P$ is at the origin $O.$ Find $x$ as a function of time $t.$
feedback.worked_solution:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14042763/assets/7bd0200a651aec7283e5c96d3cdc1589d795531e179ca0eb7cc36ef5bad8de56.png)

We're given that the velocity function $v(x)$ is

$$
v(x)=4-2x.
$$

We know that $v=\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}.$ Therefore, we have the equation

$$
\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}=4-2x.
$$

Separating the variables and integrating both sides with respect to $t,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t} & =4-2x \\ \frac{1}{4-2x}\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t} & =1 \\ \int \frac{1}{4-2x}\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,\text{d}t & =\int \,\text{d}t \\ \int \frac{1}{4-2x}\,\text{d}x & =\int \,\text{d}t \\ -\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡|2-x| & =t+K \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡|2-x| & =-2t-2K \\ 2-x & =C{e}^{-2t} \\ x & =2-C{e}^{-2t}\end{aligned}
$$

We're given that $x=0$ when $t=0.$ Therefore, $C=2,$ and the particular solution is

$$
x(t)=2-2{e}^{-2t}.
$$
